What Kind of Action Do You Want?

Most people get this part right. They come in and they say the want a pistol or a shotgun or whatever. Be as specific as you can. Maybe you want a full sized semi automatic handgun or an over under shotgun. The more specific you are the better the comments will be.

What do you want to do with this firearm?

This is one of the most important details you can include. Maybe you want a semiautomatic handgun for bullseye shooting? Maybe you want an over under shotgun for doves. This really improves the quality of the answers you get.

What is Your Price Range?

This is super important and also influences the quality of your responses. I think this is the most oft missed major factor. Let us know what you are looking to spend. Remember that holsters, slings, magazines, ammo and all that will be additional costs.

Tell Us a Little About You.

For the love of g-d and all that is holy...please do not tell us that you shot guns twice with Uncle Bubba and are now an expert.

This can really help you out. Tell us your existing preferences for what you like and what you don't like. Maybe you load 9mm and you want another 9mm. Maybe you hate manual safeties. Maybe you are left handed? Your experience level and comfort with different formats is helpful. Is this CCW? Maybe you want to talk about how you prefer to carry or what kind of clothing you wear. This is all important. Write us a book.

Respond to the Comments You Get.

Lots of countries play baseball you know. You could ask for a Japanese take perhaps. Demo mendokusai na.
Imagine watch game shows with the sound off with your back turned. It's a little like that, but less fun.

Basic goal: score more points (called runs) than the opposing team

Basic rules: 2 teams, 9 innings, 3 outs per inning, no ties

How to score? You're team bats (hits the ball) and runs around the bases (there are 3 called 1st 2nd and 3rd bases and home plate). You bat from Home plate and if you manage to touch all three bases and then return to home plate you score a run.

Defense: 9 men on the field - 1 pitcher (throws the ball to the batter), 1 catcher (returns ball to pitcher if the batter doesn't swing or swings and misses), 3 basemen (protect the area around 1st, 2nd, and 3rd), 1 short stop (fills the gap in the areas between 2nd baseman area and 3rd baseman area), 3 outfielders (spread throughout the large grassy area behind the bases usually 1 left 1 center and 1 right)

The batter gets 3 strikes to hit the ball into play. A strike is called when the batter swings and misses or the ball passes through the strike zone which is generally defined as the width of the plate and the height from the batter's armpits to his knees. If the batter accrues 3 strikes he is out. The batting team gets 3 outs in an inning. If the pitcher throws the ball outside of the strike zone it is called a "ball." In the at-bat if the pitcher throws four "balls" the batter is allowed to go to first base freely (called a "walk"). If the batter hits the ball he is supposed to run to first base. once he gets to first, he can run to second if he thinks he has time (say he hits the ball deep into the outfield). He keeps running until he stops on a base and the ball is given back to the pitcher for the next batter to come up to hit. If the next person gets a hit the person on base can continue to the next base and eventually (again if he thinks he has time) get back to home plate to score a run.

Outs: 4 ways to get outs in baseball. 1 - Strikeout: three strikes on one batter in an at-bat. 2 - Catch: If a batter hits the ball in the air a fielder can catch the ball for an out. 3 - Tag: If a base runner is not touching a base, he can be tagged by someone with possession of the ball and is considered out. 4 - Force Out: This one is a little more tricky. The basic premise is that only one runner can be on a base at a time. So, If a ball hits the ground a fielder must throw the ball to the first baseman who must catch the ball and touch 1st base before the batter reaches first base; no contact is necessary between the fielder and the batter. If there is a runner on first base, the same idea can be played at second base. If there are runners on first and second, the rule applies to third base and second base. BUT if there is only a runner at second base, he is not forced to run to the next base so he must be tagged once he is off the base to be considered out.

Innings: 9 innings are split into two half innings with each team having 3 outs to score as many runs as possible. Home team bats last (home field advantage).
